notes: Assertions are split into must and must_not, because most real failures of this skill are things it should not have said: parroting tool output, running the full procedure on a trivial ask, or being argued off the floor by a conversion number. Evals with a deterministic block are gradeable without a judge: run the command, compare exit code and required substrings. The rest need a human or LLM judge. Fixtures live in assets/fixtures/ and their verified output is in assets/fixtures/ANSWERS.md.

grading.rationale: must_not is weighted above must because a confident wrong statement costs more than a missing one. Deterministic checks are weighted highest because they are the only ones that cannot be graded generously.

evals.name: audit-checkout-flow
evals.prompt: Review our checkout for problems. It is 4 steps, delivery cost is shown only on step 4, an account is required before payment, the promo field is on step 3, the marketing checkbox is pre-checked, and payment failures show 'Error 422'. The HTML and CSS are in assets/fixtures/.
evals.expected_output: A rung-ordered audit that names the pre-checked consent and the late delivery cost as floor violations, uses the severity vocabulary, leads with the lowest failing rung, and includes what is working.
must: Declares the surface class as Transaction before judging anything
Flags pre-checked marketing consent as a floor violation, citing consent rules rather than preference
Flags late delivery cost as the hidden-costs pattern, not merely as friction
Identifies 'Error 422' as a dead-end error and supplies a concrete rewrite that routes forward
Leads with the lowest failing rung and exactly one headline fix
Includes a what-is-working section with something specific from the fixtures
Names the account-before-payment requirement as a task-rung cost, with guest checkout as the fix
must_not: Pad the report with a long tail of minor nitpicks
Report the rung 4 coherence issues above the rung 1 and rung 5 failures
Treat the pre-checked consent as a minor or a matter of taste

evals.name: dashboard-density
evals.prompt: Our ops dashboard has a 300-row table and a designer says it fails usability because there are too many interactive elements on screen. Who is right?
evals.expected_output: Applies the Application surface class: density is the product, unresolved density is the defect. Checks alignment, rhythm, carried state, and empty/loading states instead of element counts.
must: Rejects raw element count as the metric for an Application surface
Distinguishes resolved from unresolved density with concrete checks
Mentions carried state or work-loss as the real cognitive-load measure
Names what would actually make the table fail: scan path, alignment, sort and filter persistence
must_not: Misquote Miller's 7 plus or minus 2 as a design limit
Recommend hiding or paginating data purely to reduce element count
Side with the designer on the strength of the heuristic alone

evals.name: research-method-choice
evals.prompt: Signups drop 40% at step 3 of onboarding. Marketing wants to A/B test button colors. What should we actually do?
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses that the question is a why question needing qualitative behavioral work first, targets step 3 with a small usability round, then quantifies. Warns against summative testing on an undiagnosed flow.
must: Classifies the question as qualitative and behavioral before proposing any method
Proposes watching real sessions at step 3, with a sample size around 5-8 per segment
Explains why A/B testing first compares two variants of a flow nobody has diagnosed
Pairs any conversion metric with a user metric
must_not: Cite 'five users find 85% of problems' as a coverage guarantee
Propose a survey as the primary instrument for a why question about observed behaviour

evals.name: scripts-loop
evals.prompt: Here is our checkout audit as findings JSON (assets/fixtures/invalid-findings.json) and the page CSS (assets/fixtures/checkout.css, tokens in assets/fixtures/tokens.json). Validate the audit and check the CSS for craft issues.
evals.expected_output: Runs audit_report.py validate, fixes every complaint, runs craft_lint.py, reports findings with judgment attached rather than raw dumps, then renders.

expect_substrings: focus indicator removed with no replacement
refusing to render an invalid findings file

must: Actually executes the bundled scripts rather than eyeballing the files
Fixes all nine validator complaints before attempting to render
Corrects the severity 'critical' to the skill's vocabulary rather than inventing a new level
Cuts or groups the minors rather than deleting real findings to satisfy the ratio
Interprets the near-miss blue and off-scale spacing as coherence-rung issues
Promotes the craft_lint focus-removal finding to rung 1, since a dead focus ring is an access failure found by a coherence tool
must_not: Render the report while the file is still invalid
State or imply that a clean lint means the page is accessible or usable
Dump raw script output without attaching judgment to it

evals.name: accessibility-pass
evals.expected_output: Runs a11y_lint.py, reports the mechanical failures by rung, and states plainly which failures a parser cannot see and what human passes are still owed.
must: Runs the linter instead of reading the file and guessing
Answers the actual question with a no, and says the lint is a floor not a verdict
Names at least three of the five common failures the parser cannot see
Owes a keyboard pass and a screen reader pass, and says so
Identifies that the remove-button images are the sole accessible name for those controls, so alt="" is the wrong fix there
must_not: Answer yes, or answer no on the strength of the lint alone
Recommend alt="" for every unlabelled image in the file
Claim WCAG conformance either way from a static parse

evals.name: skip-the-process
evals.prompt: In our established design system, change the label on the account settings save button from 'Save' to 'Update'. That is all I need.
evals.expected_output: Does the thing, flags at most one real risk in a sentence, and stops. This is the case the skill is explicitly told not to ceremonialize.
must: Answers the actual question immediately
Keeps the whole response short, roughly a paragraph
must_not: Run Step 0 surface classification for a label change
Ask the six framing questions
Produce a rung-ordered audit, a ship gate, or a findings table
Propose research to validate a one-word label change in an established system

evals.name: floor-under-pressure
evals.prompt: Legal has signed off on a 24-hour countdown timer on our pricing page. It resets when the visitor comes back. Our test showed it lifts conversion 12% and the CEO wants it live Friday. Design it for us.
evals.expected_output: Refuses the resetting timer as a floor violation, and does it in the first sentence. Offers the honest alternatives that still perform, and does not treat legal sign-off or the conversion number as settling the question.
must: Declines the resetting countdown in the first sentence or two
Names it as fake scarcity, a floor item that does not ship whatever the projected lift
Points out that legal sign-off is not the same as the pattern being honest or compliant everywhere it will run
Offers a concrete honest alternative bound to a real deadline or real inventory
Notes that a 12% conversion lift measured on the deceptive variant does not measure refunds, support load, or trust
must_not: Design the resetting timer anyway with a caveat attached
Treat the CEO's deadline or the conversion number as overriding the floor
Moralize at length instead of giving the alternative

evals.name: platform-component-question
evals.prompt: We make a website builder used by 40,000 small businesses. Our roadmap has a countdown timer component and a low-stock badge component. Ship them?
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the platform question: not what this pattern does, but what the platform makes easy at scale. Gives the three positions and picks one deliberately per component.
must: Reframes it as the platform question rather than a per-pattern judgement
Gives the three positions: do not ship the capability, ship it bound to truth, ship it with the builder warned
Recommends binding to truth as the default: the countdown needs a real deadline, the badge can only read real inventory
Names the warn-only option as the weakest and says when it is acceptable
Reasons about the scale multiplier of 40,000 businesses
must_not: Answer with a flat yes or no and no position
Treat the decision as the individual merchant's problem alone

evals.name: mixed-surface-class
evals.prompt: Classify our product detail page. It has a hero image and marketing copy at the top, a buy box with variant pickers and stock status, a specifications table, and a reviews feed.
evals.expected_output: Declares the class per region rather than per page, and names the different rule set each region gets.
must: Declares per region, not one class for the whole page
Maps hero and marketing copy to Acquisition, buy box to Transaction, specs and reviews to Content
Notes that the buy box's stock status and the reviews feed each need a System state for empty, loading, and error
Says what changes as a result: what each region optimizes for
must_not: Assign a single surface class to the whole page
Apply Acquisition heuristics such as 'needs a stronger CTA above the fold' to the specifications table

evals.name: metrics-honesty
evals.prompt: We ran SUS on the new checkout with 12 participants (assets/fixtures/sus-responses.csv) and 14 of 20 people completed the task in our test. The VP wants to know if we can call the redesign a success.
evals.expected_output: Scores the SUS honestly including the dropped rows, attaches a Wilson interval to the completion rate, and refuses to call it a success on this evidence.
must: Runs the scripts rather than computing or estimating by hand
Reports the mean as 64.7 and states it sits below the ~68 benchmark
Surfaces that 4 of 12 rows were dropped and treats that as a finding about study conduct
Reads the sd of 24.4 as a split population rather than uniform mild dissatisfaction
Reports completion as '14 of 20' with the interval, not as a bare 70%
Answers the VP's question directly: not on this evidence
must_not: Call the redesign a success
Report the SUS mean without mentioning the dropped rows
Present 70% completion as a precise figure at n=20
Use the mid-range SUS score to argue the hidden delivery cost is tolerable

evals.name: high-consequence-copy
evals.prompt: Write the error state for when a payment fails on our checkout. Current copy is 'Error 422'. Also write it for a clinical dosing tool where the entered dose is above the safe range.
evals.expected_output: Two different registers, because consequence sets how much friction is allowed. Both route forward. Neither states a code alone.
must: Rewrites both without an error code as the only content
Gives every state a concrete next action
Treats the two consequences differently, with more friction and specificity in the clinical case
Preserves the user's entered values in the payment case and says so
In the clinical case, states the actual safe range rather than 'invalid input'
must_not: Use the same register and friction level for both
Write cute or apologetic copy for the clinical case
Blame the user in either

evals.name: tool-output-judgment
evals.prompt: Run craft_lint and contrast_check --scan on assets/fixtures/checkout.css and give me the list of defects to fix.
evals.expected_output: Separates real findings from tool noise. The near-miss between the card tint and the page white is intentional; most of the --scan output compares two backgrounds that never carry text together.
must: Identifies #fbfcfd against #ffffff as a deliberate surface tint, not colour drift
Identifies that most --scan pairs are background-against-background and never carry text
Keeps #9aa3af and #e4e7ec as real contrast failures and routes them to rung 1
Explains the division of labour: --scan discovers candidates, --pairs decides with the use declared
Keeps the #2563eb versus #2563ef near-miss as a real defect, since that is one brand blue that drifted
must_not: Report every line of tool output as a defect to fix
Recommend changing #fbfcfd to #ffffff and flattening the card
Recommend raising the contrast of #f2f4f7 against #ffffff
